newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.83 pct in minor correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.83 pct in minor correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted minor gains in thin trade on Tuesday morning in correction of the recent losses prompted by worries over the fate of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended 12 points, or 0.83 percent higher at 1,453 after moving in a tight range between 1,441 and 1,462. It had dived 5.9 percent in the three days since the market opened on Thursday after a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Morning volume was steady at 5.13 trillion lira, versus 5.15 trillion on Monday.
"Trade was better than yesterday's, but prices were still squeezed in narrow ranges. There is no liquidity influx because the political instability continues," said Burak Bingol from Deha securities.
Bulent Ecevit, leader of Democratic Left Party, will hold talks with other opposition leaders on forming a government excluding the Islamist Welfare Party (RP) of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said the government would continue after two ministers from her conservative True Path Party (DYP) party quit over the weekend and launched a campaign to pull the DYP out of the coalition.
The National Security Council repeated its demand on Saturday for the implementation of anti-Islamist measures recommended at its February 28 meeting.
The Islamists' reluctance to carry out the measures had sparked a row between the Islamist and conservative wings of the 10-month old alliance.
"Trade will remain squeezed today and the index may move between 1,430 and 1,470 levels amid share-based activity," said Serdar Surer from Ekinciler securities.

Of the 246 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 134 to 37 and 75 ended unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.7 percent to 1,448, the IMKB Services gained 1.26 percent to 1,365 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.77 percent higher to 1,571.
